'''Nicholas Cordell Collins''' (born August 16, 1983) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for seven seasons with the [[Green Bay Packers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).<ref name="FoxSport_Retirment">{{cite web |url=http://www.foxsports.com/wisconsin/story/former-packers-safety-nick-collins-officially-retires-from-nfl-081914 |title=Former Packers safety Nick Collins officially retires from NFL  |last1=Imig |first1=Paul |date=August 19, 2014 |website=Fox Sport Wisconsion |access-date=August 21, 2014}}</ref> He played [[college football]] for the [[Bethune–Cookman Wildcats football|Bethune-Cookman Wildcats]], and was selected by the Packers in the second round of the [[2005 NFL draft]]. Collins led the league in [[interception]]s returned for [[touchdown]]s and interception return yards in the [[2008 NFL season|2008 season]]. In [[Super Bowl XLV]], he intercepted [[Ben Roethlisberger]] for a touchdown as the Packers beat the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], 31–25.

In [[2011 Green Bay Packers season|2011]], Collins suffered a career-ending neck injury. He was officially released by the Packers in 2012, and formally announced his retirement in 2014. Collins was inducted into the [[Green Bay Packers Hall of Fame]] in 2016.

'''Nesby Lee Glasgow''' (April 15, 1957 – February 25, 2020) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for 14 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 1979 to 1992. He played his first nine seasons with the [[Indianapolis Colts|Baltimore/Indianapolis Colts]] and the last five with the [[Seattle Seahawks]].

Born and raised in [[Los Angeles, California]], he played [[college football]] for the [[Washington Huskies football|Washington Huskies]] in [[Seattle]] under head coach [[Don James (American football)|Don James]]. Glasgow was recognized as part of Washington's  Century Team in 1990, and was inducted in the Husky Hall of Fame in 2001.<ref name=stmobt>{{cite news |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/seahawks/former-seahawk-and-husky-standout-nesby-glasgow-dies-of-cancer-at-age-62/ |work=Seattle Times |last=Condotta |first=Bob |title=Former Seahawk and Husky standout Nesby Glasgow dies of cancer at age 62 |date=February 25, 2020 |accessdate=September 23, 2020}}</ref><ref name=sisset>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/washington/legends/services-set-for-deceased-uw-player-nesby-glasgow |publisher=SI.com |agency=(HuskyMaven) |last=Raley |first=Dan |title=Service Set For Nesby Glasgow, standout UW and Seahawks cornerback |date=March 4, 2020 |accessdate=September 23, 2020}}</ref> His  late [[Red zone (gridiron football)|red-zone]] interception helped clinch the [[1977 Washington Huskies football team|Huskies]]' upset win over third-ranked [[1977 Michigan Wolverines football team|Michigan]] in the [[1978 Rose Bowl]],<ref name=sivjj>{{cite news |url=https://www.si.com/vault/1978/01/09/822288/a-perfect-moon-shot-for-the-huskies |magazine=Sports Illustrated |last=Jares |first=Joe |title=A perfect Moon shot for the Huskies |date=January 9, 1978 |page=11}}</ref><ref name=jreswa>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=n_YjAAAAIBAJ&sjid=zu0DAAAAIBAJ&pg=6878%2C1125708 |work=Spokesman-Review |location=Spokane, Washington|last=Missildine |first=Harry |title=Jackson rescues Washington |date=January 3, 1978 |page=19}}</ref><ref name=rgros>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=q8YUAAAAIBAJ&sjid=6OEDAAAAIBAJ&pg=6858%2C593481 |work=Eugene Register-Guard |location=Oregon |agency=Associated Press |title=Huskies go from rags to roses |date=January 3, 1978 |page=1C}}</ref> was a [[Captain (sports)|team captain]] as a senior the [[1978 Washington Huskies football team|following season]].<ref name=hhfmr>{{cite news |url=https://gohuskies.com/news/2020/2/26/football-husky-hall-of-famer-nesby-glasgow-passes-away-at-62.aspx |publisher=University of Washington Athletics |title=Husky Hall of Famer Nesby Glasgow passes away at 62 |date=February 27, 2020 |accessdate=September 23, 2020}}</ref> and was first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference football teams|all-conference]] in [[1977 All-Pacific-8 Conference football team|1977]] and [[1978 All-Pacific-10 Conference football team|1978]].

Glasgow was selected in the [[1979 NFL draft#Round eight|eighth round]] of the [[1979 NFL draft]] by the [[1979 Baltimore Colts season|Baltimore Colts]], the 207th overall pick, started four games as a rookie, and became the starting free safety the [[1980 Baltimore Colts season|next year]].<ref name=indstr>{{cite news |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nfl/colts/2020/02/26/former-colts-free-safety-nesby-glasgow-dies-stomach-cancer/4883392002/ |work=Indianapolis Star |last=Newell |first=Nat |title=Indianapolis Colts first starting free safety Nesby Glasgow dies from stomach cancer at 62 |date=February 26, 2020 |accessdate=September 23, 2020}}</ref><ref name=colobt>{{cite web |url=https://www.colts.com/news/nesby-glasgow-colts-mourn-passing-jim-irsay |publisher=Indianapolis Colts |last=Walker |first=Andrew  |title=Colts mourn passing of former safety Nesby Glasgow |date=February 27, 2020 |accessdate=September 23, 2020}}</ref> In his NFL career, he amassed ten sacks and fifteen interceptions for 189 yards.  As a punt returner, he had 80 returns for 651 yards and 1 touchdown. As a kickoff returner, Glasgow had 85 returns for 1,906 yards. He was [[1984 Indianapolis Colts season|1984]] Defensive Player of the Year for the Colts and in [[1990 Seattle Seahawks season|1990]] for the Seahawks.

Glasgow died at age 62<!--on February 25,--> in 2020 after a lengthy battle with stomach cancer, which started in his stomach and liver, was at stage 4, and had already spread outside its origin.<ref name=stmobt/><ref name=sisset/> He was interred at [[Greenwood Memorial Park (Renton, Washington)|Greenwood Memorial Park]] in [[Renton, Washington]].
